definitions.explanation: The row or line at the front, whether of seats, people, or a formation.

examples.japanese: {前列|ぜんれつ}に{座|すわ}った。
examples.english: I sat in the front row.

examples.japanese: {前列|ぜんれつ}の{席|せき}はもう{埋|う}まっている。
examples.english: The front row seats are already taken.

examples.japanese: {集合写真|しゅうごうしゃしん}を{撮|と}るとき、{背|せ}の{低|ひく}い{人|ひと}は{前列|ぜんれつ}に{並|なら}んでください。
examples.english: When we take the group photo, shorter people please line up in the front row.

notes:
A straightforward compound of {前|ぜん} (front) + {列|れつ} (row, line). Used for seating, formations, and lineups.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {前列|ぜんれつ}の{席|せき}: front row seat
- {最前列|さいぜんれつ}: the very front row
- {前列|ぜんれつ}に{並|なら}ぶ: to line up in the front row
- {前列|ぜんれつ}に{立|た}つ: to stand in the front row

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {後列|こうれつ}: back row — the antonym
- {最前列|さいぜんれつ}: very front row — the superlative
- {前方|ぜんぽう}: the front (area) — refers to a general area, not a row
